answer: Bonded collateral escrows make each identity costly to operate, while shared equivocation evidence links coordinated accounts. For k identities that equivocate together, the protocol scales the base slash as O(k²), so duplicating identities raises the penalty rather than dividing it. Asymmetric depreciation compounds the loss on detection, imposing an exponential capital-loss multiplier on a sybil swarm. The canyon between honest and coordinated behavior narrows; a ledge of apparent cheapness can become a spiral of escalating losses.
